strategies.overview: Behold, the biggest tiering nightmare in Smogon history. Gothitelle used to be a valuable Pokemon in OU until Shadow Tag got banned. However, because this happened after the tiers were locked, Gothitelle got stuck into a existential limbo in the OU metagame, as it doesn't have its niche as a trapper anymore. Because of its typing, movepool, and awful stats, Gothitelle is easily outclassed by other Psychic-types like Latios, Alakazam, and Reuniclus.

movesets.name: I Wanna Be The Latios
movesets.description:
Set Description

Gothitelle is just trying to hit hard as possible with its mediocre base 95 Special Attack with this set. Psychic is your best STAB option, while Hidden Power Fighting is your only option to hit Steel-types as well as Tyranitar. Energy Ball damages bulky Ground-types like Hippowdon, Gastrodon, and Seismitoad while also being able to do a bit of damage to incoming Tyranitar that will OHKO Gothitelle with Pursuit. Dark Pulse damages other Psychic-types, and Thunderbolt can hit Skarmory. If using Energy Ball or Dark Pulse, Hidden Power Fire is the best option to hit Ferrothorn and Skarmory. Trick is your only option to not be a total momentum sucker. Seriously, never use this Pokemon. If you want a Psychic-type, a Pokemon like Latios, Alakazam, Reuniclus, Jirachi, Latias, Mew, or Victini can do way more damage or offer much more team support.

movesets.name: Shadow Tag Support
movesets.description:
• Gothitelle is the only Pokemon with Shadow Tag, giving it a unique niche in the metagame. Gothitelle excels at trapping passive Pokemon, such as Jellicent and Amoonguss, shutting them down with Taunt and effectively turning the fight into a two-on-one. That said, Gothitelle can oftentimes find itself being a liability due to its passiveness and poor damage output. Additionally, trapping is not as powerful against more offensive teams, as they can ignore Gothitelle and focus down on its teammate. Finally, the lack of reliable setup sweepers in the tier means that Gothitelle's trapping oftentimes only results in a one for one trade, which might not outweigh Gothitelle's passiveness.

  • Taunt is necessary to shut down other passive support Pokemon, such as Amoonguss and Jellicent, forcing them to use their weak attacks.

  • Trick Room is a strong speed control option, enabling Gothitelle's teammate or itself to beat opposing speed control. Helping Hand boosts the power of Gothitelle's teammate, mitigating Gothitelle's low damage output. Skill Swap can be used to give a teammate Shadow Tag, take away crucial abilities from the foe, such as Prankster from Thundurus, or reset abilities so they can be activated again, such as Intimidate. Giving a teammate Shadow Tag also allows Gothitelle to switch out to a more offensive teammate, mitigating its lackluster damage output.

  • A Calm nature ensures that Gothitelle survives a Dragon Gem Latios's Draco Meteor with the rest dumped into Defense so that it can better tank strong physical attacks, such as Tyranitar's Crunch.

  • Gothitelle is best when trapping support Pokemon, so foes must be wary that Gothitelle can hard switch into them.

  • Setup Pokemon, such as Suicune and Ferrothorn, are great teammates alongside Gothitelle because it can prevent the foe from switching from an unfavorable matchup, allowing its teammate to freely set up. Rain teams benefit greatly from Gothitelle's trapping because it can shut down Amoonguss and Jellicent, two common rain answers, allowing its teammate to remove them thus opening the door for Kingdra to sweep. Landorus-T is another excellent teammate, as U-turn allows Gothitelle to be brought in safely. Additionally, Gothitelle can use Skill Swap on Landorus-T, reactivating Intimidate and further weakening the opposing physical attackers. Finally, Pokemon with strong attacks, such as Dragon Gem Latios and Choice Band Kyurem-B, can benefit from Shadow Tag, allowing it to take out a crucial target.

  • Other set options include Trick with Choice Scarf or Choice Specs. The idea is similar in that Gothitelle aims to shut down a passive support Pokemon by giving it a Choice item with Trick while trapping it but is typically less consistent due to Gothitelle needing to Trick away its item before it is able to support its teammate.

strategies.overview: Although nowhere near as bulky as the metagame's premier Psychic-type, Cresselia, Shadow Tag gives Gothitelle an incredible niche in the format. With it, Gothitelle can tactically pin and eliminate key threats to its team's endgame as well as enabling the Perish trap archetype in its entirety. Gothitelle, however, is a one trick pony, as its offensive movepool is not deep enough to leverage and its natural bulk is not sufficient enough to invest into its modest Special Attack; both of these are true for Cresselia.

movesets.name: Shadow Tag Trapper
movesets.description:
• Gothitelle's main goal is to stay on the field and provide whatever support it can to its teammates. To this end, defensive moves like Rest and Protect are necessary to keep it alive and keep opposing Pokemon trapped.
  • Psychic and either Trick Room or Thunder Wave give Gothitelle the ability to exert some pressure on the field by threatening chip damage or speed control.
  • Gothitelle's EVs are dumped into its bulk, allowing it to comfortably live most major hits like Dragon Gem Draco Meteor from Latios and then recover back with Rest.

Other Options

  • Skill Swap lets Gothitelle pass its ability to its partner, creating potentially unwinnable game states for the opponent as they stare down a Shadow Tag Ferrothorn or Suicune. Both of these Pokemon are naturally very bulky, have setup moves, and can be impossible walls to break through if the right opposing Pokemon are trapped.
  • Gothitelle gets numerous interesting support moves, such as Safeguard, Charm, and Tickle, to support its team.
  • Other items like Sitrus Berry, Leftovers, and Lum Berry can also fit on Gothitelle as needed and allow it to run the aforementioned support moves.

Common Partners

  • Scrafty supports Gothitelle by threatening one of its biggest threats in Tyranitar, mitigating the damage from Landorus-T through Intimidate, and aiding in Trick Room going up with Fake Out.
  • A Perish Song user, most commonly Politoed, is required for a Perish trap team.

Checks and Counters

  • Thundurus is not threatened by Gothitelle and can use Taunt to prevent it from setting up Trick Room or paralyzing its partner.
  • Dark-types such as Tyranitar and Scrafty are immune to Gothitelle's Psychic and 2HKO with Crunch.
  • Landorus-T nearly 2HKOes Gothitelle with U-turn, which also switches itself out of the effects of Perish Song.
  • Volcarona, particularly Bug Gem sets, is capable of OHKOing Gothitelle and eliminating it as a potential threat.

strategies.overview: Gothitelle is a fairly decent Pokemon; however it lacks many of the important traits it needs to compete with many of the other Psychic-types in the VGC 2011 metagame. Despite this, it provides a bit of originality and can offer some surprise factor.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Gothitelle can also run an excellent support set. With access to both Reflect and Light Screen, Gothitelle, equipped with Light Clay, can set up screens that give your team the ability to tank hits. It also gets Rain Dance, which it can set up to help teammates who can take advantage of it. Gothitelle also has access to Thunder Wave and Toxic, which can harm opponents greatly throughout the match.

Checks and Counters

Gothitelle's main counters are nearly anything that can resist both Psychic and Shadow Ball. Notable ones are Scrafty, Krookodile, and Hydreigon. Without proper support, Gothitelle will be totally walled by these powerful Pokemon. Its checks are bulkier Ghost-types as well as others who can shrug off Psychic and Shadow Ball. Jellicent, Tornadus, Thundurus, Landorus, and many of the commonly seen offensive Pokemon can bother Gothitelle. It also does not resist the very common move Heat Wave, Water Spout, Surf, Rock Slide, and Earthquake that are all around the VGC metagame.

movesets.name: Trick Room
movesets.description:
Gothitelle's best use in VGC is as a Trick Room starter. With fairly decent stats, Gothitelle takes many hits and dishes back some pain. Outside of Trick Room, however, Gothitelle can really fall short, so it's important to try and get it up quickly. Its bulkiness is what makes it somewhat useful, as this allows for it to take even super effective hits with ease and set up.

Gothitelle has decent enough coverage in order to make it a worthwhile try on any aspiring Trick Room team. With STAB Psychic, many of the common Fighting-types such as Terrakion and Conkeldurr fear it. Shadow Ball allows for coverage against Ghost-types who may threaten Gothitelle in certain situations. Protect is a golden move in VGC, allowing Gothitelle to not only scout its opponent's item with Frisk, but also take advantage of seeing one of its moves.

Gothitelle tends to be outclassed by both Reuniclus and Musharna. Reuniclus boasts a higher Special Attack and HP stats, as well as lower speed, making it a better candidate to set up and sweep. Musharna also is bulkier than Gothitelle, and has a higher Special Attack stat, which also makes it a stronger Trick Room starter. However, Gothitelle has more special bulk than both of them, allowing it to tank hits. It is also much less used, which can catch opponents off guard. Overall, Gothitelle doesn't have much to use to damage the opponent, which can leave it in a bad position in the game. More often than not, Gothitelle can be dead weight, but if supported right it can be a great set up Pokemon.
